fictional_reviews.text: Fictional review: the pop-up book folding up ahead of my kart never got old, and the Bosphorus bridge at dusk is gorgeous for code-drawn paper. Four chapters and a real Grand Prix kept me playing.

Fictional review: made-up weekend player note, charming paper look and fun drift boosts, but the karts feel light and I wanted online multiplayer or a battle mode. Great for a few cups with the family.
Invented dev-fan take: zero asset files, everything generated in code, 60 fps on high with auto-scaling and a deterministic autopilot playtest? As a technical achievement this is pure joy.

how_to_play: Open https://burakerdemci.github.io/kagit-kart/ in a desktop or phone browser and click/tap to start (also unlocks audio).
Pick a mode: four-chapter Grand Prix, single race, or time trial against your own ghost; then paper-weight speed class (80 g, 120 g, 200 g) and driver.
Steer with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight or A/D (left stick on gamepad, on-screen controls on phone); accelerate with ArrowUp/W, brake with ArrowDown/S.
Hold Space/Shift (RB on gamepad) while steering to drift and release for tiered mini-turbo boosts; drive over boost pads and hit ramps for trick boosts.
Grab items and fire with X/E (X or LB on gamepad); race 3 laps against 7 AI rivals, follow the minimap, and finish first. Pause with Esc/P, mute with M.
mechanics: Pop-up-book tracks that fold up out of the page ahead of the karts
Four chapters with distinct print styles (meadow, Bosphorus dusk, glacier pass, ruled-notebook desk)
Eight drivers with individual stats (1 player + 7 CPU rivals)
Eight items including fountain-pen rockets, bubble gum, paper planes, inkwell, cellophane shield, scissors
Three-tier drift mini-turbo boosts plus slipstream, ramp tricks, and boost pads
Three modes: four-chapter Grand Prix, single race, time trial with ghost
Paper-weight speed classes 80 g, 120 g, 200 g
Paper-crane respawn after falling off the page
Procedural soundtrack with per-chapter themes that speed up on the final lap
Four quality levels with automatic resolution scaling

rating.reason: Excluding the target, closest comparators are Kart Royale (50 overall: single-track 3D kart loop), Turbo Kart Rally (40: single-circuit procedural kart racer), Sakura Rally (56: multi-stage rally with campaign/open world), and Gale Kart (54: 8-track kart package with no verified screenshots). Kagit-Kart exceeds the single-track kart games on scope (4 chapters, Grand Prix + single race + ghost time trial, 8 drivers, 8 items, 3 speed classes, drift tiers, slipstream, tricks, procedural music) with 9 inspected runtime screenshots showing a coherent original paper art style, plus documented QA (27-issue playtest, 5 fix rounds) and an automated 60-fps autopilot acceptance run. It trails moorestech (64, co-op server, modding, years of scale) and Meridian Wake (60) on systems breadth and multiplayer, and sits near LUMENRIFT (58) rather than above it: live play was not performed, so playability, performance, and balance are not proven beyond stills and docs, and there is no human multiplayer.

reconstructed_prompt: Build Kagit-Kart, a Mario Kart-style 3D kart racer in Three.js that takes place inside a pop-up book, with zero asset files: every mesh, paper texture, letter, sound, and music bar generated in code. Include 4 chapters (daisy meadow, Bosphorus dusk with suspension bridge, glacier pass, writing-desk notebook road), 8 paper drivers with stats, 8 stationery items, Grand Prix / single race / ghost time trial modes, 80/120/200 g speed classes, 3-tier drift boosts, slipstream, ramp tricks, crane respawn, podium ceremony, Turkish UI, keyboard + gamepad + touch controls, procedural Web Audio soundtrack, and auto quality scaling, playable in the browser.

screenshot_based_score.reason: Best inspected gameplay frames (meadow countdown with 4+ karts, glacier drift with purple boost shards, bridge crossing, notebook-desk corner) show a coherent original cut-paper style with halftone textures, full race HUD (lap, timer, position, minimap), and varied chapters. Below Kart Royale (70) and Turbo Kart Rally (70) on scene density, lighting richness, and texture detail; near Sakura Rally (68) and LUMENRIFT (68) on stylized coherence. Discounted menu/title/podium/intro frames as non-gameplay; stills prove nothing about motion or feel.

source_analysis.finding: Repository BurakErdemci/kagit-kart is public with description 'A kart racer inside a pop-up book. Every mesh, paper texture, letter and sound is generated by code; no asset files. Play in the browser.' and homepage pointing at the submission URL; primary language JavaScript.

Play page hosts the actual game: page root #kk-root with canvas, Turkish boot card 'Kagit Kart / sayfalar aciliyor', import map for three.js, and module boot from ./src/main.js with a load-failure message path.

Game is a kart racer: four chapters (Papatya Cayiri meadow, Bogaz Gecesi Bosphorus dusk with suspension bridge, Buzul Gecidi glacier pass, Yazi Masasi writing desk on ruled-notebook road), eight drivers with stats, eight items, three modes (four-chapter Grand Prix, single race, time trial with ghost), 80/120/200 g speed classes, 3-tier drift boosts, slipstream, ramp tricks, crane respawn, podium ceremony, procedural soundtrack.
Keyboard controls documented: steer Left/Right or A/D, accelerate/brake Up/Down or W/S, drift Space/Shift, use item X/E, look back C, pause Esc/P, mute M.
Gamepad controls documented in the same table: steer left stick; accelerate/brake A or RT, B or LT; drift RB; use item X or LB; look back Y; pause Start.
Touch controls supported: README states 'On a phone, the game shows on-screen controls' and the play tagline reads '(desktop or phone, keyboard, gamepad or touch)'.
Single human player: roster is '8 karts (1 player + 7 CPU)' and time trial is 'against your own ghost'; no local or online multiplayer is documented.
Playable URL verified: README 'Play it in your browser' link targets the submission URL, which serves the game boot page rather than a repo or promo page.
Engine/version: import map pins three to 0.186.0 from jsdelivr for both 'three' and 'three/addons/'; the game is the sole dependency besides generated code.
Codebase is plain ES modules with no build step (~27,000 lines of JavaScript in 78 modules); local run is a static server plus an optional Playwright playtest harness.
Audio is synthesized at runtime: sequencer plays a per-chapter theme with final-lap tempo rise and all sound effects synthesised; no audio asset files exist.

Creation attribution: owner briefed Claude (Opus 5.5, in Claude Code) with a single 'make a Mario Kart-like racing game' brief under a no-outside-assets rule; subagents wrote feature lanes, a QA agent filed 27 issues, five fix rounds followed.

No catalog match: no existing games/ directory or catalog entry references this repository, playable URL, or project; closest catalog entries are other kart racers (Kart Royale, Turbo Kart Rally, Gale Kart, Wouf Kart) with different repos and URLs.

Evidence gaps: gh CLI had no token in this environment so GitHub evidence was gathered via the public REST API and raw file fetches instead of `gh api`; the live build was not played, so playability, performance, and balance rest on docs, screenshots, and the reported automated playtest, not on hands-on verification. No source-code behavior beyond inspected docs/config was invented.
